An angry mob in Ilesa, Osun State, has beaten a survivor of a road accident to death after the crash claimed the lives of two pedestrians. The mob also set the vehicle involved in the accident ablaze. Reacting, the Osun State Police Command condemned the incident, warning residents against taking the law into their hands. The police spokesperson, Abiodun Ojelabi, disclosed this in a statement obtained in Osogbo on Thursday. Ojelabi said the accident, which occurred on Tuesday, involved an unregistered Toyota Camry, a TVS motorcycle and two pedestrians identified as Silas Seun and Matthew Dada. He said, “The unfortunate incident resulted in the immediate death of the two pedestrians at the scene of the accident. The driver of the vehicle, one Favour Fabunmi, ‘M’, 23 years old, and other occupants of the Toyota Camry were successfully rescued alive. “However, in a disturbing turn of events, one of the rescued occupants was attacked and severely beaten by an angry mob. He was subsequently rushed to the hospital but was later confirmed dead. The vehicle was also set ablaze by the mob and completely burnt to ashes.” ASUP begins strike in four South-West states over unpaid allowances Tinubu, South-West govs invited to Adeleke’s second-term inauguration Adeleke appoints new monarch for Esa-Oke Ojelabi said the case had been transferred to the command headquarters for a comprehensive investigation, adding that legal procedures had been initiated. He quoted the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Zungura, as saying he “strongly condemns the act of mob violence and warns members of the public against taking the law into their own hands.” The CP urged residents to “resist the temptation to administer instant justice, irrespective of the circumstances, and allow the appropriate authorities to investigate and handle reported offences in accordance with the law.” He also assured the public that the command would leave no stone unturned “in identifying all individuals who participated in the mob action, and anyone found culpable will be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law.” Ojelabi urged residents to remain calm and law-abiding, advising them to report accidents and criminal incidents to the nearest police station rather than resorting to violence. The PUNCH had earlier reported that the police in Osun commenced an investigation into the killing of Monica Mary, a student of Westland University, Iwo, who was allegedly stabbed to death by unknown assailants.
